summary: Holloman Air Force Base (HMN/KHMN) is a United States Air Force installation located near Alamogordo in south-central New Mexico, situated at the western edge of the Tularosa Basin. It is home to the 49th Wing and hosts the unique German Air Force Flying Training Center, where Luftwaffe pilots train on the F-16 Fighting Falcon alongside their USAF counterparts. The base has a rich aviation heritage dating back to World War II and is closely tied to the adjacent White Sands Missile Range and White Sands National Park.
faqs:
Q: What military units are stationed at Holloman Air Force Base?
A: The 49th Wing is the primary host unit, operating MQ-1 Predator and MQ-9 Reaper remotely piloted aircraft, and providing training for F-16 pilots. The German Air Force's Flugausbildungszentrum (Flying Training Center) is also based here.

Q: Can civilians use Holloman Air Force Base airport?
A: The airfield is primarily a military installation, but limited civilian access may be available with prior coordination. Most travelers visiting the Alamogordo area use nearby commercial airports like El Paso International.

Q: What is nearby Holloman Air Force Base?
A: The base is adjacent to White Sands Missile Range and White Sands National Park, with the Sacramento Mountains and the city of Alamogordo just minutes away. It is also within driving distance of Carlsbad Caverns National Park.

Q: When was Holloman Air Force Base established?
A: The base was originally established in 1942 as Alamogordo Army Air Field and was renamed Holloman Air Force Base in 1948 in honor of Colonel George V. Holloman, a pioneer in rocket-powered aircraft research.
transport_tips: The base is accessible via U.S. Highway 70 and is approximately 90 miles northeast of El Paso International Airport. Visitors without military ID should arrange passes in advance through their sponsor, as base access requires proper credentials. Rental cars are available in Alamogordo for local travel.
local_tip: Time your visit around sunrise or sunset to witness the remarkable views of the White Sands dunes glowing pink and orange from the base's perimeter—the contrast against the Sacramento Mountains makes for an unforgettable sight that even locals stop to appreciate.
